exercise_bank.title: Count It Out
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the numbers out loud from 1 to 20, one at a time, at a steady pace.

exercise_bank.title: Days in Order
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the days of the week out loud in order, starting with Sunday.

exercise_bank.title: Months in Order
exercise_bank.instructions: Say the months of the year out loud in order, starting with January.

exercise_bank.title: Name What You See
exercise_bank.instructions: Look at an object near you right now. Say its name out loud, then say one word that describes it.

exercise_bank.title: Picture in Your Mind
exercise_bank.instructions: Picture a kitchen in your mind. Name out loud three objects you would expect to find there.

exercise_bank.title: Three Words, One Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Here are three words: dog, park, morning. Say one full sentence out loud that uses all three.

exercise_bank.title: Can't Find the Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Think of the word for the tool you use to cut paper. If it doesn't come right away, describe out loud what it does and what it looks like, then say the word.

exercise_bank.title: Category Rapid Fire
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud as many animals as you can in twenty seconds.

exercise_bank.title: Write the Numbers
exercise_bank.instructions: Write the numbers 1 through 20 in order, then read your list back out loud.

exercise_bank.title: Write the Days
exercise_bank.instructions: Write out the days of the week in order, starting with Sunday.

exercise_bank.title: Write the Months
exercise_bank.instructions: Write out the months of the year in order, starting with January.

exercise_bank.title: Describe It in Writing
exercise_bank.instructions: Look at an object near you. Write one sentence describing what it looks like and what it is used for.

exercise_bank.title: Build a Written Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Here are three words: quickly, umbrella, rain. Write one full sentence using all three.

exercise_bank.title: Write Then Add a Detail
exercise_bank.instructions: Write down the name of an object you can see right now. Underneath it, write one detail describing its color or shape.

exercise_bank.title: One-Step Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this instruction, then do it: touch your nose.

exercise_bank.title: Two-Step Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this instruction, then do both parts in order: clap your hands, then touch your knee.

exercise_bank.title: Three-Step Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this instruction, then do all three parts in order: stand up, turn around once, then sit back down.

exercise_bank.title: Find the Match
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this description: it is round, orange, and you peel it before eating it. Point to or name the object being described.

exercise_bank.title: Yes or No Listen
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this sentence: The sun is cold at night. Say out loud whether that is true or false.

exercise_bank.title: Where Is It
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this instruction, then do it: put your hand under the table.

exercise_bank.title: Between and Behind
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to this instruction, then do it: place one object behind another object near you.

exercise_bank.title: Listen and Answer
exercise_bank.instructions: Listen to these two sentences: Maria packed her bag. She was going on a trip. Answer out loud: what was Maria doing?

exercise_bank.title: Read and Do
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this instruction, then do it: tap the table three times.

exercise_bank.title: Read Two Steps
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this instruction, then do both parts in order: pick up a pen, then set it down on your left.

exercise_bank.title: Match the Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this word: chair. Point to or find a matching object nearby.

exercise_bank.title: Read and Point
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this description: it has four legs, a back, and people sit on it. Point to the object being described.

exercise_bank.title: Read the Direction
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this instruction, then do it: place your hand between two objects on your desk.

exercise_bank.title: Read and Answer
exercise_bank.instructions: Read these two sentences: Tom forgot his umbrella. It started to rain on his walk home. Answer out loud: what problem did Tom have?

exercise_bank.title: Tongue Press Hold
exercise_bank.instructions: Press your tongue firmly against the inside of your cheek, hold for three seconds, then relax. Repeat five times on each side.

exercise_bank.title: Lip Round and Spread
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'oo-ee-oo-ee' out loud, rounding your lips fully on 'oo' and spreading them fully on 'ee'. Repeat ten times.

exercise_bank.title: Full Jaw Open and Close
exercise_bank.instructions: Open your jaw slowly as wide as is comfortable, then close it slowly. Repeat five times, then say 'ah' with a fully open jaw.

exercise_bank.title: Half-Speed Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this sentence out loud at half your normal speed, giving every word its own clear space: I would like a glass of water, please.

exercise_bank.title: Overarticulate Every Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, exaggerating every consonant more than feels natural: The big black cat sat on the mat.

exercise_bank.title: Louder Than Usual
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud at a volume noticeably louder than your normal speaking voice, without shouting: My voice is strong and clear today.

exercise_bank.title: Tap to Pace
exercise_bank.instructions: Tap the table once for each word while you say this sentence out loud, keeping every tap evenly spaced: I am speaking one word at a time.

exercise_bank.title: One Breath, One Phrase
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a breath, then say this short phrase out loud in one breath: I feel good today. Pause, take another breath, and repeat it twice more.

exercise_bank.title: Soft Start
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, starting the very first sound gently and gradually instead of with a hard push: Amazing things can happen today.

exercise_bank.title: Light Touch Consonants
exercise_bank.instructions: Say these words out loud using a light, relaxed touch on the first sound instead of pressing hard: pat, bat, top, dot.

exercise_bank.title: Link It All Together
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this phrase out loud as one continuous flow of sound, without stopping airflow between words: I want to go outside and play.

exercise_bank.title: Stretch Every Syllable
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud, stretching each syllable slightly longer than usual: We are walking to the store together.

exercise_bank.title: Chunk and Breathe
exercise_bank.instructions: Say this sentence out loud in three short chunks, taking a breath between each: I woke up early / and made breakfast / before school.

exercise_bank.title: Slow and Smooth Passage
exercise_bank.instructions: Read this passage out loud at a deliberately slower, smoother pace than normal: The morning sun rose over the quiet hills as birds began to sing.

exercise_bank.title: Pause and Restart Gently
exercise_bank.instructions: If a word ever feels stuck while you talk, pause fully for one second, then restart just that word slowly and gently before continuing.

exercise_bank.title: One Minute Easy Talk
exercise_bank.instructions: Talk out loud for one minute about your morning, using a soft gentle start on the first word of every sentence.

exercise_bank.title: Ask It Back
exercise_bank.instructions: Answer this out loud: what did you eat for breakfast? Then ask the same question back as if talking to a friend.

exercise_bank.title: Stay on Topic
exercise_bank.instructions: Pick a topic, like your favorite weekend activity. Talk out loud about it for three back-and-forth exchanges without changing the subject.

exercise_bank.title: How Do They Feel
exercise_bank.instructions: Imagine a friend just lost their favorite toy. Say out loud how they probably feel, and explain why you think that.

exercise_bank.title: Read the Expression
exercise_bank.instructions: Think of someone smiling with their arms crossed. Say out loud what you think that expression and posture might mean.

exercise_bank.title: Introduce Yourself
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud an introduction of yourself to someone new, including your name and one thing you enjoy doing.

exercise_bank.title: Join the Game
exercise_bank.instructions: Imagine some kids are playing a game at the park. Say out loud what you would say to politely ask to join in.

exercise_bank.title: Ask for a Repeat
exercise_bank.instructions: Imagine someone spoke too quietly for you to understand. Say out loud a polite way to ask them to repeat themselves.

exercise_bank.title: Tell It in Order
exercise_bank.instructions: Think of three things you did this morning, in order. Tell them out loud as a short story with a clear beginning, middle, and end.

exercise_bank.title: Gentle Hum Warm-Up
exercise_bank.instructions: Hum gently for five seconds, feeling a light buzzing or vibration around your lips and nose.

exercise_bank.title: Hum Into a Word
exercise_bank.instructions: Hum gently, then let the hum flow directly into the word 'hello' out loud, keeping that same forward, buzzy feeling.

exercise_bank.title: Sustain the Sound
exercise_bank.instructions: Take a comfortable breath, then hold a steady 'ee' sound out loud for as long as you comfortably can, without straining.

exercise_bank.title: Pitch Glide Up
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'ee' out loud, sliding your pitch smoothly from low to high like a gentle siren going up.

exercise_bank.title: Pitch Glide Down
exercise_bank.instructions: Say 'oh' out loud, sliding your pitch smoothly from high to low like a gentle siren going down.

exercise_bank.title: Strong Short Bursts
exercise_bank.instructions: Say short, firm 'ee' sounds out loud at a few different comfortable pitches, keeping each one clear and easy, not strained.

exercise_bank.title: Vocal Habits Check-In
exercise_bank.instructions: Say out loud how much water you drank today and whether you did any shouting or a lot of throat-clearing.

exercise_bank.title: Carry the Buzz Into a Sentence
exercise_bank.instructions: Hum briefly, then say this full sentence out loud keeping that same easy, forward, buzzy voice feeling the whole time: My voice feels easy and comfortable.
